LingoSparkHow to use this plan

How to use this plan

1. Set a schedule

Look at the calendars and the weekly template. Spread the 14 topics across the time you have until May 2027. Leave weeks for revision.

2. Learn by topic

Each CKE module has a mind-map page, notes, and a vocabulary checklist. Understand the theme first, then learn words in example sentences.

3. Track progress

After each review, tick the box next to a term. Copy stubborn items onto “Words to revisit”.

4. Train every paper

Matura Extended tests listening, reading, Use of English, a 200–250-word text, and a spoken exam. Vocabulary supports every part.

5. Review on a cycle

Return to each topic every 2–4 weeks. In the last six weeks, go through every checklist again.

6. Use LingoSpark

Paste ENG–PL lists into the free vocab games at https://lingospark.study. Longer writing practice lives in Writing Suite.

Matura Extended English — exam map

PaperWhat to practiseMy notes / score
1. Listeningmain idea, detail, speaker’s attitude, matching, multiple choice
2. Readinglonger texts, matching headings, true/false/not given, multiple matching
3. Use of Englishword formation, transformations, cloze, collocations, B2 grammar
4. Writingopinion / for-and-against essay, article, formal letter, review — about 200–250 words
5. Speakingwarm-up, picture description, follow-up questions, a longer turn on a stimulus

My goals for this school year

Vocabulary source: 14 thematic modules from the CKE informator for Matura (extended level). Lists are B2, not the Grade-8 packs.

LingoSparkSchedule · full plan

Suggested schedule to May 2027

Adjust the pace to your calendar. Calm pace: about two topics a month plus reviews.

Full plan (two years) — September 2025–May 2027 — about two topics a month and a quarterly review. Best if you start in the second-to-last year of liceum.
September–October 2025 — People; Home and living. Review all tenses; start a word-formation notebook.
November 2025–June 2026 — Education → Health (topics 3–11). Each month: vocabulary + one paper (L / Rd / W / Sp).
September–November 2026 — Science and technology; Nature; The state and society. Recycle every checklist.
December 2026–January 2027 — Grammar, transformations, phrasal verbs, stubborn terms.
February–March 2027 — CKE sample papers: listening, reading, Use of English.
April–May 2027 — Light revision, timed writing, speaking sets. Stay calm.

My own dates — full plan

LingoSparkSchedule · intensive plan

Intensive plan (start September 2026 — exam May 2027)

If you are in the final year, keep this pace: two to three topics a month plus reviews.

September–October 2026 — Topics 1–4 + tense review (including perfect and continuous forms).
November–December 2026 — Topics 5–8 + conditionals, wish, passives.
January–February 2027 — Topics 9–14 + reported speech, inversion light, word formation.
March–April 2027 — Sample papers, 200–250-word texts, speaking sets.
May 2027 — Light review, sleep, exam-day plan.

Grammar checklist — Matura Extended (1/2)

Tick ☐ when you can use the structure in a sentence and spot it in a Use of English task.

☐AreaMy note / example
Present / past / future — all simple, continuous and perfect forms
including present perfect continuous
Future perfect & future continuous
By June I will have finished. / This time tomorrow I will be sitting the paper.
Used to / would / be used to / get used to
I used to live… / I am used to waking up early.
Modals of deduction (present & past)
must / might / can’t + have + past participle
Mixed conditionals & wish / if only
If I had revised, I would be calmer now.
Passives in all tenses + have something done
I’m having my essay checked.
Reported speech & reporting verbs
admit, deny, suggest, warn, accuse of
Relative clauses — defining & non-defining
whose, where, of which; commas
Gerunds vs infinitives (B2 pairs)
regret doing / forget to do / stop to do
Articles, quantifiers, uncountables
the environment, advice, a piece of research

Tenses and time

☐Structure / ruleExample / note
Present Perfect vs Past Simple
I have lived here for years. / I lived there in 2019.
Present Perfect Continuous
I have been revising since Monday.
Past Perfect for earlier past
She had left before the exam started.
Future continuous
This time next week I will be travelling.
Future perfect
By May I will have finished every checklist.
be going to vs will vs present continuous for future
plans, predictions, arrangements
used to vs would (past habits)
would not with states
be used to / get used to + -ing
I am used to writing 250-word essays.

LingoSparkGrammar — detail

Modals, conditionals, the passive

☐Structure / ruleExample / note
must / might / can’t + be (present deduction)
She must be tired.
must / might / can’t + have + pp (past deduction)
He can’t have forgotten the date.
should have / ought to have (regret)
I should have started earlier.
needn’t have vs didn’t need to
needn’t have = did it, but it was unnecessary
Zero / first / second / third conditionals
Mixed conditionals
If I had slept, I would feel better now.
wish / if only + past / past perfect / would
I wish I knew. / I wish I had known.
Passive of all tenses
The results will be published tomorrow.
have / get something done
I had my passport renewed.

Writing checklist — 200–250 words

☐Text typeRemember
Opinion essay (rozprawka)
clear thesis, 2–3 arguments, conclusion
For-and-against essay
both sides, then your position
Article
title, hook, register for a magazine / school paper

Dear Sir or Madam / Yours faithfully
Review
title of the work, opinion + justification

aim 200–250; plan before you write
Register
no slang in formal tasks; no contractions in letters

Speaking checklist — oral exam

☐SkillNote
Warm-up answers in full sentences
not one-word replies
Picture description

Follow-up questions
justify with because / that’s why
Longer turn on a stimulus
structure: intro → 2 points → conclusion
Opinion language
I would argue that… / It seems to me that…
Asking the examiner to repeat
Could you repeat that, please?
